FCMB Group Plc’s profit before tax doubled to N272.8bn in the nine months ended September 2026, supported by higher interest income, improved margins and a reduction in funding costs. The financial services group disclosed this in its unaudited financial results for the period released on Friday, showing a 102.8 per cent increase from N134.5bn recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. Profit after tax rose by 85.7 per cent to N232.9bn from N125.5bn, while gross earnings increased by 21 per cent to N1tn from N828.1bn. The growth in earnings was driven by a 23.4 per cent increase in interest income and a 10.7 per cent expansion in earning assets to N5.43tn from N4.90tn. Net interest income grew by 52.3 per cent to N534.2bn from N350.8bn, as the group benefited from higher interest income and a three per cent decline in interest expenses. FCMB Group attributed the reduction in interest expenses to an improved mix of low-cost deposits and lower cost of funds, which helped raise its net interest margin to 12.3 per cent from 10.1 per cent. Operating expenses increased by 12.5 per cent to N268.9bn from N239bn, slower than the growth in earnings, reflecting cost discipline and efficiency gains from digital transformation. The group’s cost-to-income ratio consequently improved to 43.5 per cent from 55.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The group said the third quarter benefited from a N9bn net write-back. The Nigerian banking subsidiary’s non-performing loan ratio increased to 6.4 per cent from 4.7 per cent in June 2026, reflecting a 13 per cent reduction in the loan book during the third quarter and new Stage 3 classifications. The group’s annualised return on equity strengthened to 30.1 per cent from 22.4 per cent, while return on assets rose to 3.9 per cent from 2.3 per cent. FCMB Group’s total assets grew by 9.7 per cent to N8.37tn at the end of September from N7.63tn in December 2025. Loans and advances to customers, however, declined by 8.3 per cent to N2.17tn from N2.37tn, as repayments by corporate customers outweighed growth in retail and small and medium-sized enterprise lending. The group’s total equity rose by 47.8 per cent to N1.24tn from N836.4bn, supported by retained earnings and a capital injection of about N227bn during the first quarter of 2026. Its capital adequacy ratio stood at 24.6 per cent at the end of September, while assets under management increased by 23 per cent to N2.1tn from N1.7tn in December 2025. The banking group contributed 80 per cent of the group’s profit before tax, with earnings rising by 94 per cent to N216.9bn. The non-banking businesses and holding company accounted for the remaining 20 per cent, recording a combined profit before tax of N55.9bn, up 147 per cent year-on-year. Speaking on the results, the Group Chief Executive, Ladi Balogun, said the performance reflected efforts to improve efficiency, strengthen earnings capacity and enhance the quality of growth through digital transformation and portfolio rebalancing. He said the group expected earnings momentum to continue in the fourth quarter, supported by lower operating expenses following the full recognition of the 2026 AMCON levy in the nine-month results and seasonal growth in digital lending and payments. Balogun added that the group’s nine-month return on equity of about 30 per cent was expected to push its full-year performance materially above its earlier guidance of 25 per cent. He said this would provide a foundation for further profitable growth and shareholder value creation.
